The player's gaze moves from their hands to the audience beyond the stage. The last notes of the guzheng solo fade into the concert hall. Applause rises, then dissolves into the soft sound of a phone notification.

The image changes from the concert hall to the player's bedroom. The guzheng case is open beside the desk. Several worn synthetic finger picks rest on a folded cloth.
Reminder: please prepare a reliable new set of guzheng finger picks before next month's examination. Comfort and fit matter more than appearance.

The player opens a marketplace app and searches for guzheng finger picks. Most results are labelled synthetic resin, plastic, or imitation tortoiseshell. One heavily advertised listing uses the words “玳瑁古筝义甲” and claims that the material is genuine.
Two routes appear. At this point, the player is shopping normally and does not yet know what “玳瑁” means.

It is genuine hawksbill, a traditional material. Customers often choose it for its firm feel. This size should suit you.

The player has not researched the word “玳瑁” and does not interpret the purchase as risky or unusual.

Several days later, the package arrives. The material name “玳瑁” is printed on the label inside the box. The picks feel firm and unfamiliar. Out of simple curiosity about what the material name means, the player decides to look it up online.

I just got this set! Tried it during practice today — it feels pretty good. The listing calls it ‘玳瑁’. Have you tried this kind?

In this route, the friend bought the set. The player has only the shared photo, messages, and listing screenshot.

The computer screen lights the room. In Route A, the product label rests beside the keyboard. In Route B, the friend's screenshot remains open on the phone. Curiosity — not suspicion — leads the player to search the meaning of “玳瑁”.

“玳瑁” is the Chinese name for the hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata), a marine animal whose shell has historically been used to make decorative objects and small accessories.

The hawksbill turtle is listed as a Class I national key protected wild animal in China. A product description or photograph still cannot prove that this item is genuine hawksbill. The report must separate claims from verified facts.

Preserve what already happened. The player has bought the item. Capture the existing listing, conversation, transaction and package records; stop using the item and keep it secure. Do not make another transaction or confront the seller.

Preserve what already happened. The friend bought a set, but the player has only the shared photo, messages and listing. Do not buy the product to obtain additional evidence, and do not invent or access the friend's private order records.
A report form opens beside the evidence folder. Attach only records the player actually possesses, in a traceable order. The form does not write an accusation automatically.

A report form opens beside the evidence folder. Attach only the messages and images the friend shared, the listing record and the official species source. Do not invent or automatically access the friend's private order records.

At 19:42 on 18 June 2025, I purchased guzheng finger picks advertised and recommended as “genuine hawksbill.” After receiving the item, I searched the material name out of curiosity and learned that the hawksbill turtle is nationally protected. I have stopped using the item. I have not independently verified its material.

At 20:06 on 18 June 2025, a friend sent me a photo and an online listing for finger picks advertised as “genuine hawksbill.” My friend said they had bought the set and found it good to use. I did not purchase the product and have not independently verified its material or my friend's purchase.
Report submitted. Save the reference number and keep the evidence unchanged.

Your report has been received. The information may be reviewed or forwarded to the relevant department. This acknowledgement does not confirm the material, establish wrongdoing, or guarantee a particular enforcement outcome.

A safe synthetic set rests beside the strings. The player puts it on and begins to play. The sound is ordinary, clear, and enough.

The last guzheng note fades into the clicking of a keyboard. The camera cuts to a cramped packing room, behind a man at his desk. The shop avatar matches the listing seen earlier.

BUYER: Is this the same material as the one in your listing?

SELLER: Yes, genuine hawksbill. It is in stock. I can send it tomorrow.

He sends the reply, seals another packet, and places it on a growing stack. This audience-only scene is not evidence in the player's report.

MONTHS LATER. Brief, silent shots show investigators comparing transaction records, a specialist examining seized material, and an evidence folder being closed. Cut back to the packing room. Police officers are present. An officer closes handcuffs around the seller's wrists.

This depicts the fictional seller being taken into custody, not a conviction or the automatic result of one report.

HAWKSBILL TURTLE / 玳瑁

The hawksbill turtle is a protected marine animal. A product description or visual resemblance cannot by itself establish what a product is made from. When an unfamiliar animal-derived material appears in a product description, pause and check official sources.

One report may not end an illegal trade. It can still provide a useful lead when it is accurate, complete, and responsibly submitted.
